correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet barycentric Gram matrix and its rank-one inverse give K(x,y)=A(A+1)sum_i x_i y_i/alpha_i−A and exact affine reproduction. The pointwise norm is strictly vertex-maximal by a strict-integral triangle inequality. Each vertex integral reduces to F_A(alpha_i) via a beta tail and truncated first moment. Gamma splitting constructs E[Z_a|Y_b]=Z_b when a<b, and positive probability mass across zero makes Jensen strict. Fixed-budget balanced minimax follows from min_i alpha_i≤A/m. Gamma(a)/a converges to zero in probability and a bounded negative-part argument gives nonattained supremum 1+2A. The beta CLT plus uniformly bounded scaled second moments proves the sqrt(A) prefactor. All finite and limiting quantifiers are explicit; 241 deterministic checker assertions passed, but finite checks are not proofs.

originality.rationale: The examined degree-one Dirichlet reproducing kernel (Griffiths–Spanò, 2013) and known symmetric/simplex special cases do not state or by themselves imply that smaller individual Dirichlet shape yields a strictly larger endpoint projection norm across *unequal* probability measures. The proof supplies the missing beta-gamma conditional martingale coupling, identifies exactly all worst vertices, solves the fixed-total concentration minimax and boundary extremal problem, and establishes an asymptotic outside the symmetric formulas. Targeted published-finding corpus searches and full-text comparisons found no statement of these additional implications. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Priority is not certified: a preexisting result under beta convex-order, multivariate Jacobi or weighted Lebesgue-function terminology could imply the same comparison.

Independent scientific and bibliographic reviews have not been performed.

value.rationale: Stability of a weighted affine least-squares projector depends on an entire allocation of Dirichlet mass. The exact two-norm formula and strict smallest-shape vertex rigidity solve the natural arbitrary-weight optimization, give a unique balanced design minimizing worst-case amplification at fixed concentration, and quantify a sharp nonattained boundary cost. The conditional beta-convex-order lemma and Gaussian concentrated-law regime expose genuine structural behavior not contained in the published uniform-weight or symmetric-parameter tables; this is a substantive sharp optimization invariant rather than a cosmetic substitution.
